bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, execution-focused, and visionary. Emphasizes 'structural' margin improvements over cyclical gains. Strong emphasis on strategic alignment with US critical mineral goals to de-risk DRC exposure. Celebratory of market cap milestone (INR 1 Lakh Cr).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The US-DRC critical mineral agreement (Dec 2025) is a key de-risking factor for their Congo assets, positioning Lloyds as a non-Chinese alternative for US supply chains. The take-or-pay nature of the Tata Steel pipeline asset generates disproportionate free cash flow relative to sustaining capex. BHQ beneficiation not just a volume play but a significant royalty tax arbitrage.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "All the expansion plans are drawn with the most efficient capital allocation"; the deck cites FY26 average RoCE of 56% (ex CWIP) and average RoE of 37%.
- IPS (capital subsidy): entitled to receive refund of State GST and royalty on captive ore consumed.
- Consolidated net D/E moved from -0.17 (FY23), -0.10 (FY24), 0.00 (FY25) to 1.20 (FY26) as the capex cycle was funded; standalone net debt as on 30.06.2026 stated at INR 56,161 mn, and TEIPL net debt (incl RPS) as on 30.06.26 at INR 58,205 mn.
- Renewable SPV structure chosen for capital efficiency: "Exposure is limited to a minority equity stake, not full project capital expenditure", with captive tariff fixed for 25 years insulating from DISCOM tariff revisions and exemption from cross-subsidy and additional surcharge; stated savings of INR ~620 Mn in year 1 and INR ~14.5 Bn over 25 years by SPV.
- Consolidated networth rose from 15,290 (FY23) to 28,108 (FY24) to 64,601 (FY25) to 1,42,661 INR Mn (FY26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- High-grade hematite ore (~63% Fe average) with mining lease valid until CY2057 and a zero-premium payment obligation to the Government of Maharashtra for the entire lease period - a structural cost advantage versus competitors facing re-auction at higher premiums
- Large geological resource base of 863 million tonnes (157 MnT DSO + 706 MnT BHQ) supporting mine life well beyond CY2030, when more than 80 MTPA of competing industry capacity is expected to come up for re-auction
- Genuinely end-to-end integrated ferrous value chain (captive mining through beneficiation, pelletisation, DRI, captive power, slurry pipeline logistics) that eliminates external raw-material dependencies and reduces exposure to intermediate product price cycles
- Rapid step-up in value-added product (VAP) share: VAP contributed 32% of standalone revenue and 30% of standalone EBIT in FY26, up from 20% of revenue and 11% of EBIT in FY25
- 85 km Hedri-Konsari slurry pipeline lowering logistics cost and reducing dependence on road transport for ore evacuation
- Annuity-like earnings stability from the MDO (Mine Development and Operations) subsidiary Thriveni, which operates on long-tenure, fee-based contracts with blue-chip clients, insulated from commodity price movements
- Proven execution track record: pellet plant, DRI units and the slurry pipeline were each commissioned ahead of or on schedule, with the first pellet plant completed in 16 months and reaching 100% utilisation within 4 months
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global steel demand and commodity-cycle exposure — Management flags global steel demand dynamics, economic slowdown and market volatility as key risks facing the Company, given its revenue base is still weighted to iron ore and steel-linked products.
- Rising finance costs and increasing leverage — Management explicitly flags rising finance costs as a key risk. The FY26 Key Financial Ratios disclosure shows Debt-Equity Ratio rising to 0.47x from 0.16x (+201% YoY) on increased borrowings, Current Ratio falling to 0.87x from 1.62x (-46%) on higher current liabilities, and Debt-Service Coverage Ratio falling to 1.35x from 8.37x (-84%), consistent with the Company funding a large capex programme partly through debt.
- Raw material price volatility — The Company flags potential constraints or significant increases in raw material prices as a key risk to profitability.
- Regulatory and approval delays / policy risk — Operations, ongoing projects and profitability may be impacted by delays in government approvals and procedural processes, or unfavourable changes in government policy relating to mining, allocations and tariffs.
- Labour law, safety and workforce risk — The mining and steel industries operate under stringent labour and health-and-safety regulations; any safety lapse could damage property, assets and human capital, and labour shortages could adversely impact operations and ongoing projects.
- Environmental and carbon/water regulatory risk — Rising environmental concerns and regulatory requirements relating to carbon emissions and water availability may impose operational constraints that could impact the Company's growth trajectory.
- Social licence to operate / regional unrest risk — The Company operates in a socio-economically sensitive region (Gadchiroli/Chandrapur, Maharashtra); any unrest in the region could adversely affect mining operations.

outlook.body:
- Scale Capacity Expansion - pursuing a phased capacity expansion programme spanning mining, beneficiation, pellets, integrated steel and copper, executed through disciplined planning and standardised project delivery to build a larger, more efficient operating base.
- End-to-End Value Integration - transforming from an iron-ore-only miner into a fully integrated metals and mining enterprise across beneficiation, pelletisation, steel manufacturing and copper, reducing dependence on a single revenue stream and improving cost control, margin stability and supply security.
- Diversified Resource Portfolio - broadening the resource base beyond iron ore through entry into copper and cobalt and recurring Mine Development and Operations (MDO) contracts, reducing concentration risk and creating multiple growth engines.
- Logistics Cost Optimisation - redesigning the logistics network (principally slurry pipelines) to reduce structural freight costs, dependence on road transport, weather-related disruptions and carbon emissions, while supporting higher production volumes.
- Sustainable Operations Integration - embedding sustainability into strategic and operational decisions via equipment electrification, renewable power, slurry pipelines and waste-to-energy systems to lower emissions while improving productivity.
- Global critical-minerals diversification - entry into copper marks a step towards a future-ready portfolio aligned with global electrification and decarbonisation trends, participating in growing demand for critical minerals as a resource provider.
- MDO annuity-earnings strategy - leveraging Mine Developer and Operator engagements (through subsidiary Thriveni) for stable, annuity-like revenues that reduce overall portfolio cyclicality and align with India's focus on domestic coal production and energy security.
- Dividend decisions are governed by a formal Dividend Distribution Policy adopted under the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The Board determines dividend for a period after considering the Company's financial performance, advice of Executive Management, and stated capital allocation plans - including expected cash requirements for working capital, capital expenditure in technology and infrastructure, general corporate purposes, and investments required towards execution of the Company's strategy - balancing shareholder distribution against reinvestment needs. For FY26 the AGM notice records a resolution to declare a dividend of Rs 1 per equity share of face value Rs 1.

outlook.body: LMEL is executing a multi-year forward-integration programme, transitioning from a merchant iron ore miner to an integrated, low-cost steel producer via a phased programme spanning BHQ beneficiation, large-scale pelletisation, expanded DRI manufacturing and eventual long/flat steel capacity. Completed in FY26: the 85 km Hedri-Konsari slurry pipeline (Line 1, 10 MTPA) fully operational; the first 4 MTPA Pellet Plant (Plant 1) at Konsari, commissioned and completed in 16 months from construction start, reaching 100% annualised capacity utilisation within four months; and the 360 KTPA DRI expansion at Ghugus, commissioned in Q2 FY26. A second 4 MTPA pellet plant at Konsari (Plant 2) was commissioned in May 2026, just after FY26 close. Under construction/planned: a 1.2 Million Tonne Wire Rod, Blast Furnace and Coke Oven integrated steel plant (board-approved October 2023 and January 2024) comprising a sponge iron plant (2x500 TPD), captive power plant, EAF-based SMS (2x50T), ladle refining furnaces (2x50T), a vacuum degassing unit (1x50T), an RHF (120 TPH), a wire rod mill (2x600,000 TPA) a blast furnace (840,000 TPA) and a coke oven (400,000 TPA) - construction has commenced and the project is at an advanced stage; a third 4 MTPA pellet plant (Plant 3) and associated slurry pipeline at Ghugus, with land procured and Environmental Clearance in hand, construction commenced in Q4 FY26 and commissioning expected in FY27; and a parallel 195 km slurry pipeline under development that will add ~16 MTPA of evacuation capacity (taking total pipeline evacuation capacity to ~26 MTPA) and extend the network to Chandrapur. Separately, the Company is diversifying into critical minerals through a 50% stake in the operational Surya Mines platform and a 49% stake in the Chemaf Group, both in the DRC, targeting a combined pathway to ~100,000 TPA copper and ~20,000 TPA cobalt capacity, and is scaling its MDO subsidiary (Thriveni) into new mineral categories (coal, copper, bauxite) and international contracts. outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic steel demand is expected to remain infrastructure-led, supported by the Government of India's long-term capacity targets of 300 million tonnes by 2030 and 500 million tonnes by 2047, though capacity utilisation across the industry will depend on the pace of demand absorption.
- The Company expects to benefit from rising domestic steel demand and a global upcycle in iron ore, supported by its strong resource base and expanding mining capacities.
- Global refined copper consumption is projected to grow to 28.66 million tonnes in 2026 and 29.24 million tonnes in 2027 (International Copper Study Group), driven by electrification, renewable energy, EVs and data centres - a structural demand tailwind cited in support of the Company's copper diversification.
- India's coal sector is expected to sustain strong production growth toward 1.15 billion tonnes, reinforcing energy security and supporting stable, annuity-like MDO revenue for the Company.
- Forward integration into beneficiation, pelletisation, DRI and steel is expected to enable value capture across the entire chain, enhancing margins and reducing exposure to commodity price volatility, aided by logistics investments such as slurry pipelines that strengthen cost competitiveness and supply reliability.
- The Company has been named a preferred partner for the Panguna mine in Bougainville, Papua New Guinea, and is advancing community-focused initiatives there, including a proposed 100-bedded hospital, alongside this opportunity.
- Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) engagements, conducted through subsidiary Thriveni, provide stable, annuity-like revenues under long-tenure, fee-based contracts across India and internationally.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: LMEL mines high-grade hematite iron ore at its Surjagarh Iron Ore Mine (SIOM) in Maharashtra and converts a growing share of it into value-added products - sponge iron (DRI), iron ore pellets and captive power - through its Ghugus and Konsari facilities. The Company operates two business segments, Mining and Value Added Products, and is extending its integrated model internationally through stakes in copper-cobalt assets in the Democratic Republic of Congo and through its mine-development-operator (MDO) subsidiary, Thriveni.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic steel demand is expected to remain infrastructure-led, supported by the Government of India's long-term capacity targets of 300 million tonnes by 2030 and 500 million tonnes by 2047, though capacity utilisation across the industry will depend on the pace of demand absorption.
- The Company expects to benefit from rising domestic steel demand and a global upcycle in iron ore, supported by its strong resource base and expanding mining capacities.
- Global refined copper consumption is projected to grow to 28.66 million tonnes in 2026 and 29.24 million tonnes in 2027 (International Copper Study Group), driven by electrification, renewable energy, EVs and data centres - a structural demand tailwind cited in support of the Company's copper diversification.
- India's coal sector is expected to sustain strong production growth toward 1.15 billion tonnes, reinforcing energy security and supporting stable, annuity-like MDO revenue for the Company.
- Forward integration into beneficiation, pelletisation, DRI and steel is expected to enable value capture across the entire chain, enhancing margins and reducing exposure to commodity price volatility, aided by logistics investments such as slurry pipelines that strengthen cost competitiveness and supply reliability.
- The Company has been named a preferred partner for the Panguna mine in Bougainville, Papua New Guinea, and is advancing community-focused initiatives there, including a proposed 100-bedded hospital, alongside this opportunity.
- Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) engagements, conducted through subsidiary Thriveni, provide stable, annuity-like revenues under long-tenure, fee-based contracts across India and internationally.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: LMEL is executing a multi-year forward-integration programme, transitioning from a merchant iron ore miner to an integrated, low-cost steel producer via a phased programme spanning BHQ beneficiation, large-scale pelletisation, expanded DRI manufacturing and eventual long/flat steel capacity. Completed in FY26: the 85 km Hedri-Konsari slurry pipeline (Line 1, 10 MTPA) fully operational; the first 4 MTPA Pellet Plant (Plant 1) at Konsari, commissioned and completed in 16 months from construction start, reaching 100% annualised capacity utilisation within four months; and the 360 KTPA DRI expansion at Ghugus, commissioned in Q2 FY26. A second 4 MTPA pellet plant at Konsari (Plant 2) was commissioned in May 2026, just after FY26 close. Under construction/planned: a 1.2 Million Tonne Wire Rod, Blast Furnace and Coke Oven integrated steel plant (board-approved October 2023 and January 2024) comprising a sponge iron plant (2x500 TPD), captive power plant, EAF-based SMS (2x50T), ladle refining furnaces (2x50T), a vacuum degassing unit (1x50T), an RHF (120 TPH), a wire rod mill (2x600,000 TPA) a blast furnace (840,000 TPA) and a coke oven (400,000 TPA) - construction has commenced and the project is at an advanced stage; a third 4 MTPA pellet plant (Plant 3) and associated slurry pipeline at Ghugus, with land procured and Environmental Clearance in hand, construction commenced in Q4 FY26 and commissioning expected in FY27; and a parallel 195 km slurry pipeline under development that will add ~16 MTPA of evacuation capacity (taking total pipeline evacuation capacity to ~26 MTPA) and extend the network to Chandrapur. Separately, the Company is diversifying into critical minerals through a 50% stake in the operational Surya Mines platform and a 49% stake in the Chemaf Group, both in the DRC, targeting a combined pathway to ~100,000 TPA copper and ~20,000 TPA cobalt capacity, and is scaling its MDO subsidiary (Thriveni) into new mineral categories (coal, copper, bauxite) and international contracts. FY24-FY26 cumulative capital expenditure was stated in the narrative as part of this programme (rupee quantum not reproduced here; see NAMED DISCLOSURE handling).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- High-grade hematite ore (~63% Fe average) with mining lease valid until CY2057 and a zero-premium payment obligation to the Government of Maharashtra for the entire lease period - a structural cost advantage versus competitors facing re-auction at higher premiums
- Large geological resource base of 863 million tonnes (157 MnT DSO + 706 MnT BHQ) supporting mine life well beyond CY2030, when more than 80 MTPA of competing industry capacity is expected to come up for re-auction
- Genuinely end-to-end integrated ferrous value chain (captive mining through beneficiation, pelletisation, DRI, captive power, slurry pipeline logistics) that eliminates external raw-material dependencies and reduces exposure to intermediate product price cycles
- Rapid step-up in value-added product (VAP) share: VAP contributed 32% of standalone revenue and 30% of standalone EBIT in FY26, up from 20% of revenue and 11% of EBIT in FY25
- 85 km Hedri-Konsari slurry pipeline lowering logistics cost and reducing dependence on road transport for ore evacuation
- Annuity-like earnings stability from the MDO (Mine Development and Operations) subsidiary Thriveni, which operates on long-tenure, fee-based contracts with blue-chip clients, insulated from commodity price movements
- Proven execution track record: pellet plant, DRI units and the slurry pipeline were each commissioned ahead of or on schedule, with the first pellet plant completed in 16 months and reaching 100% utilisation within 4 months

non-obvious takeaways: The US-DRC critical mineral agreement (Dec 2025) is a key de-risking factor for their Congo assets, positioning Lloyds as a non-Chinese alternative for US supply chains. BHQ beneficiation not just a volume play but a significant royalty tax arbitrage.
